answer: Real coverage overlaps: a phone at a boundary hears two or three neighbouring cells at once, and the verifier builds a graph of which cells are ever heard together, checking each claim against the map. A pulse of genuine overlap data shows which neighbours truly coexist, while an anchor of invented neighbours fails when the graph shows those cells never overlap in reality. A voyage through a city produces a rich, varied overlap graph, but a farm's devices all report the same small neighbour set, and that sameness is the tell.
